- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent trend, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent trend, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overbought bias.  
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (forecast > true by >5%) are common; cap forecast at 5% below true peak for next 3–5 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 3–5% above 10-day moving average, reduce by 1–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in first 5 days, assume momentum bias and reduce subsequent forecast by 0.5–1% daily.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.2–0.4) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid sentiment misalignment.
